class.name: OrthoplexCellMeshND
class.brief_description: An ND cell mesh representing an orthoplex.
class.description: OrthoplexCellMeshND is a class for generating cell meshes representing orthoplexes, also known as the ND cross-polytope. All of its vertices exist at plus or minus the half-extents along each axis, and its cells are all simplex cells. Orthoplexes exist in all dimensions, and are the dual of boxes (square/cube/tesseract). The 2D version of an orthoplex is a diamond (square rotated 45 degrees), which has 4 vertices (-X, +X, -Y, +Y) and 4 edges in each quadrant. The 3D version of an orthoplex is the octahedron, which has 6 vertices (-X, +X, -Y, +Y, -Z, +Z) and 8 triangular faces in each octant. The 4D version of an orthoplex is the 16-cell or hexadecachoron, which has 8 vertices (-X, +X, -Y, +Y, -Z, +Z, -W, +W) and 16 tetrahedral cells.

method.name: from_orthoplex_wire_mesh
method.description: Creates an orthoplex cell mesh from [OrthoplexWireMeshND]. The orthoplex cell mesh will have the same size and material as the wireframe mesh.

method.name: to_orthoplex_wire_mesh
method.description: Converts this orthoplex cell mesh to a [OrthoplexWireMeshND]. The wireframe mesh will have the same size and material as the cell mesh.

members.member: The dimension of the orthoplex. This is calculated as the length of [member size]. Setting this will resize [member size] to the new dimension.

The half-extents of the orthoplex in meters, also known as just "extents". This is the "radius" of the orthoplex, the distance between each vertex and the center. This is a wrapper around [member size] for situations where you want to use the extents instead of size.

The size of the orthoplex in meters. This is the axis-aligned "diameter" size of the orthoplex in ND space, where each component is the distance between opposite vertices. This is the value that is stored internally.
